summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Introduced in House):

blocks.text: This bill requires public electric utilities to use the best-available transmission conductor for certain interstate transmission lines (i.e., power lines) in order to recover the costs of the conductor through consumers' electric bills.

Specifically, in any filing seeking to recover the costs of a transmission conductor for the transmission line and in any proceeding to determine if the costs may be recovered through rates, the bill directs the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to presume that (1) the use of a best-available transmission conductor is a prudent practice and that the associated costs are just and reasonable, and (2) the use of a transmission conductor that is not a best-available transmission conductor is not prudent and that the associated costs are not just and reasonable.

A best-available transmission conductor is a conductor that (1) provides the greatest feasible and commercially available energy-carrying capacity at a given voltage level, (2) provides the highest feasible and commercially available electrical efficiency at that voltage level, and (3) mitigates thermal sag (drooping of power lines) at the maximum rated transmission-carrying capacity of the facility.
The bill applies to projects to (1) construct new transmission facilities; or (2) modify, upgrade, or replace an existing transmission line.

This bill would require public electric utilities to use the best-available transmission conductor, the cable that carries electricity, on certain interstate power lines if they want to recover the cost of that cable through consumers' electric bills.

When a utility asks to recover these costs, or when the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission decides whether the costs can be passed on through rates, the Commission would presume that using a best-available conductor is a sensible practice and that its costs are fair and reasonable. It would presume the opposite for any conductor that is not the best available: that using it is not sensible and its costs are not fair and reasonable.

A best-available conductor is one that can carry the most electricity possible at a given voltage, that does so as efficiently as is feasible and commercially available, and that limits thermal sag, the drooping of power lines caused by heat, at the line's maximum rated capacity.
The bill applies to projects that build new transmission lines or that modify, upgrade, or replace existing ones.
